comments.text: The Devil’s Den is even more disturbing when you know more about this area. Locals don’t go out hiking during this time of year and that time of day because it’s too hot. The temp could have been in the 90s with humidity making it feel like the 100s. Locals who want to do this either do it in the spring or fall or in the early mornings. My family and I talked about it after the attacks because we couldn’t believe someone would lie in wait all day waiting for someone and how crazy that person must be. Waiting in the middle of nowhere with the humidity just for the right party to walk by. It would have been mostly empty except for tourists or die hard hikers. McGann really wanted to make it isolated before he attacked. Everyone I know believes he intended to kidnap the girls. The whole area just wants him to get “strung up” and stop wasting everyone’s time with pleading not guilty.

comments.text:
The first story really stuck with me because where he was at is very indigenous and the four arrows really stand out. He was between the towns of Port Angeles and Forks, WA (made infamous from Twilight). À LOT of people still travel up there for the novelty of it and i imagine they’re not always good guests… trespassing, leaving trash, etc. I know there are a lot of people who don’t mind it, but some want the peace of their area back.

Some of these lands are heavily federally protected Native American lands. Not just reserves, but lands tied to spiritual practices. Some of these lands are prohibited from being trespassed by anyone, for any reason, period. 

Four arrows in à line is often seen as a boundary; both a line in the sand and a warning saying “these are private lands. We see you here. This is your last warning— dont cross this line.” It can also represent a line of protection… basically drawing a line near his things to prevent evil or ill intent from following him; but no one would’ve known he was missing at that time so I think that particular symbolism is unlikely. 

Those lands are also extremely dense, with difficult, mountainous, terrain, and EXTREMELY easy to get disoriented in. People get lost 5 feet off the road. And honestly, I think that’s what happened. He was near a lot of natural beauty… waterfalls, lakes, etc. I think he wanted to have a short hike and took limited gear, spreading his gear out to grab only a few items bc it’s very secluded and hed be back soon ro put it back away. Then he got lost. 

It would make sense to head to the highest ground like he was found so he could see the way out. Unfortunately the weather shifts quick and the highest ground is colder with less protection. He probably got soaked and died of hypothermia within a day or two. Perhaps a local saw his stuff spread out right after he left and either knew hiking was dangerous and left four arrows as a protector or left them as a warning not to leave a mess and trespass again. Either way it’s a sad reminder to never underestimate Mother Nature. 🤍
